Resources · Impeccable · 03
Impeccable · pbakaus/impeccable
Give the agent a design vocabulary
Models learned from the same SaaS templates, so unguided UI shares the same tells.
The AI tells it flags
Inter (or a system font) for everything
Purple-to-blue gradients
Cards nested inside cards
Gray text on colored backgrounds
Bounce and elastic easing
1 skill
/impeccable <command> <target>
24 commands
polish, audit, critique, distill, bolder, quieter, harden…
62 detector rules
Deterministic, no LLM or API key. Also as CLI, CI check and Chrome extension.
PRODUCT.md + DESIGN.md
init records audience and constraints; document records the visual system.

Resources · Impeccable · 04
Impeccable · Best-practice order
Set up once, polish last
Five stages from the super-board map. Fix and style commands run only when needed.
1 · Setup
init · document · extract
→
2 · Plan / build
shape first, then build
→
3 · Diagnose
critique + audit
→
4 · Fix & style
harden layout typeset animate…
→
5 · Finish
polish, always last
terminal
npx impeccable install
/impeccable init
/impeccable critique landing
Tip: use one design skill at a time. Overlapping design skills pull the agent in different directions.
Shortcut: /impeccable pin audit gives you /audit.

super-board · EricTechPro/super-board
Kanban in, merged PRs out
An orchestrator drains your board: Build → QA → Review, then merge when checks pass.
Ready card
A ticket with clear acceptance criteria
→
/super-build
Worktree, smallest safe change, tests, draft PR
→
/super-qa
Evidence and screenshots, or bounce back to Build
→
/super-review
Own hypotheses, remembers past findings
→
Merge gate
Your verify_commands pass on the reviewed commit
6 guard hooks
Block worktrees outside .claude/worktrees, reading secrets, writing live API keys, deletes outside the project, pushes to main.
Model routing
Haiku grades each card. Easy goes to Sonnet, medium to Opus, hard to your session model. --low and --high shift the ladder.

Resources · Skill packs · 09
super-board · /super-qa
QA that brings evidence
Runs as the QA lane in a board run, or alone as a bug-bash. Point it at staging, not production.
One test per criterion
Written where the defect lives: Vitest for unit or integration, Playwright only when the browser broke.
Test-gap check
Maps each criterion to tests and hunts edge cases with exact values. High gaps are written red-first.
Evidence in the PR
Screenshots at desktop, tablet and mobile, plus logs and HARs, embedded in the PR comment.
Files it, never hides it
Problems outside the ticket become source:qa cards instead of silent fixes.
terminal
# standalone bug-bash
/super-qa
/super-qa 5
/super-qa --resume
/super-qa --continue-on-error

Topic 04
Watching your agents
When several sessions run at once, know who is working and who is waiting on you.
Resources · Agents · 16
Podium · eengelking/podium
One tab for every session, subagent and fork
Free and MIT-licensed, for one developer or a whole team.
Single pane of glass
Model, context fill, cost and branch per session. Waiting ones turn amber.
Drill into subagents
A row per subagent and fork with its own tokens and cost.
Answer from the browser
See the last 20 tool calls and reply when a session waits on you.
Why a mod, not a hook
Settings hook: session, model, waiting or ended. No tokens, cost or context fill, and no heartbeat.
Mod podium-reporter: runs inside Claude Code and sees each request's token usage. Sessions show up in about 2 s.
Links  Podium launch post · github.com/eengelking/podium
Scale solution
Plugin
Resources · Agents · 17
Podium · Security
Answering a session is off by default
Anyone who can answer can type into your session, so it sits behind several locks.
Five switches
A server token, two Admin toggles and two mod options must all be on.
Per-session level
off · questions · questions-and-plans · everything
Allow once only
"Always allow" and slash commands stay in the terminal.
Owner or Admin
192-bit tokens, stored as hashes, tied to one name.
Pull, never push
The mod fetches answers. Nothing in a session listens on a port.
Secrets redacted
sk-ant- keys and Bearer values are replaced before sending.
Install: podiumctl start, then /plugin install podium-reporter@eengelking-marketplace.
Links  Security section of the post
Resources · Agents · 18
Our own hook · Chrome DevTools MCP
Auto-close Chrome after agent browser tests
A global Stop hook that closes the DevTools MCP browser when each Claude reply ends.
Problem
Agents leave Chrome open after tests. One window stayed open for 12 hours.
→
Root cause
One browser per session, and nothing closed it until the session ended.
→
Fix
A Stop hook that closes only the Chrome this session started.
→
Result
Closes after each reply, reopens on the next call. Your own Chrome is never touched.
~/.claude/settings.json
"Stop": [{ "hooks": [{
  "type": "command",
  "command": "[close-session-chrome script]"
}]}]
Global: it lives in your user settings, so every project gets it.
Safe: it only kills the browser this session launched, never yours.
Habit
Hook

Reverse Engineer Anything
See a feature you like in someone else's app. Learn how it works, with evidence.
Resources · REA · 20
REA · morluto/rea
A bridge between your agent and real RE tools
REA is not a decompiler. It gives the agent one MCP interface to Ghidra, Hopper, IDA and built-in analyzers, and returns evidence with every finding.
Decompile
Inspect the target without its source code
→
Understand
Trace the code path; context carries across tool calls
→
Recreate
Write your own version and test it against the original
What it can analyze (selection)
Native binaries · Ghidra, Hopper, IDA
JavaScript & Electron
Websites · Chrome
Network captures · HAR
.NET assemblies
Android APKs · JADX
Firmware
PyInstaller apps

Resources · REA · 21
REA · Setup
Install REA, then give it a decompiler
Setup registers the MCP server and workflow instructions for your agent, with backups. Restart the agent afterwards.
terminal
# needs Node 22.23.4+, 24.22.1+ or 26.12.1+
npx rea-agents setup
# optional: the rea command
npm install --global rea-agents
rea --help
Native targets need a provider
Ghidra, Hopper or IDA. Setup can install Hopper with your approval. JavaScript analysis needs none.
Linux note
Ghidra and JS analysis need a procps-compatible ps on the PATH.
Our install prompt: “Install REA with all required steps. Also install Ghidra. Is the decompiler installed? Check the config and verify it.”
Links  rea.tools · github.com/morluto/rea
Resources · REA · 22
REA · Live demo
Rebuild a simpler PDF compressor
Target: smallpdf.com/compress-pdf. We send three prompts and watch the subagents work.
1 · Install
“Install REA from github.com/morluto/rea and do all required steps. Also install Ghidra.”
2 · Verify
“Is the decompiler installed? Also check the config and verification.”
3 · Investigate and build
“Use the REA skill and several subagents. Reverse engineer smallpdf.com/compress-pdf, find its stack, and build a simpler tool: compress a PDF without changing its content, then save.”
Watch for: the evidence and the unknowns in each finding. REA cannot hand back the original source code.

Resources · REA · 23
REA · Before you use it
Four limits to plan around
The video's main advice: gather evidence, follow it, then build something new and test it.
No original source
You get pseudocode, structure and evidence, not the author's code.
Prompt injection
Text inside the target can try to steer your agent. Treat it as data.
Not a sandbox
Runtime capture runs the target with your user permissions.
Legal use only
Research, interoperability, preservation, or software you own or may examine.
Data: whatever the agent reads from the target goes to your model provider. Do not point it at client binaries without approval.
Links  REA disclaimer · Video: limits and legality

Case study: launch capacity
How an agent load-tested vortibhai.com before launch, and what it found.
Resources · Case study · 25
Case study · Vortibhai launch capacity
Go, with one condition
Ready for a normal launch of up to about 800 users at once. Fix capacity before a 2,000-user peak day.
620,830
requests across 7 k6 runs
0 errors
500 users for 10 min, p95 586 ms
~470 req/s
where the API stops scaling (≈ 800 users)
0.38%
timeouts at a 2,000-user spike; back to normal 40 s later
Setup: Spring Boot on one EC2 host with Redis and MongoDB Atlas M0, Nuxt SSR on Vercel Hobby. Load from one Mac in Dhaka.

Scale solution
Resources · Case study · 26
Case study · What the agent found
Findings, most important first
Each finding names its file and line, and says what was measured and what was inferred.
Area
Finding
Next step
Capacity
Throughput stops at ~470 req/s, even with 95% Redis hits.
Re-run the stress test while watching docker stats; put a CDN on public GETs.
Latency
Every call from Bangladesh costs at least 275 ms; the server is in us-east-1.
A server or CDN closer to users.
Backend
Empty AI summaries are never cached; a new FAQ clears the whole list cache.
Cache the empty result; evict one entry.
Frontend
Mobile /search LCP is 4.4 s; mobile main thread blocked 400–800 ms.
Cut unused JavaScript.
Security
2 issues found while reading the code.
Fix before launch.
